study.title: Acupuncture-assisted lifestyle intervention improve the metabolic status and spontaneous brain activity of type 2 diabetes Mellitus patients: a randomized, clinical trial
study.study_design: single-blind randomized clinical trial with sham acupuncture control
study.randomization: computer-generated list, 1:1 ratio; independent mathematician used R 4.0 to generate randomized sequence according to order of participant enrollment; third party concealed allocation sequence in sealed opaque envelopes
study.blinding: single-blind; participants, data collection staff, and data analysts blinded to treatment assignments; acupuncturist aware of group assignments prior to treatment
study.disease_condition: type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), overweight or obese
study.inclusion_criteria: Diagnosed with T2DM presenting 1 or more of: (1) fasting plasma glucose (FPG)>=7.0 mmol/L, (2) 2-h plasma glucose (2-h PG) value during a 75-g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT)>=11.1 mmol/L, (3) random plasma glucose>=11.1 mmol/L; overweight or obesity defined as BMI>=24 kg/m2 or >=28 kg/m2; age from 18 to 70 years old; voluntary informed consent
study.exclusion_criteria: pregnancy and lactation; long-term courses of hormone drugs or weight loss supplements; severe organic diseases such as advanced tumor, cardiac, hepatic, renal, or mental diseases; unfit to receive treatment of acupuncture

arms.dropouts: 10 discontinued: Covid-19 (n=3), Time Conflict (n=4), Travel (n=2), Undesired efficacy (n=1)

interventions.stimulation_type: electroacupuncture at selected points; manual acupuncture at remaining points
acupoints_used_exact: Renying (ST9, level with the tip of and 1.5 cun lateral to the laryngeal prominence)
Shuitu (ST10, 1 cun down from ST9, on the anterior border of sternocleidomastoideus muscle)
Liangmen (ST21, 4 cun above the midline of the umbilicus, 2 cun lateral to the anterior midline of the abdomen)
Tianshu (ST25, 2 cun lateral to the midline of the umbilicus)
Guilai (ST29, 4 cun below the midline of the umbilicus, 2 cun lateral to the anterior midline of the abdomen)
Zusanli (ST36, 3 cun below the lateral depression of patellar ligament, one finger width lateral from the anterior crest of the tibia)
Fenglung (ST40, 8 cun superior to the tip of the external malleolus, two finger width lateral from the anterior crest of the tibia)
Neiting (ST44, Proximal to the web margin between the 2nd and 3rd toes, at the junction posterior to the toe web of the red and white skin)
interventions.anatomical_location_exact: Foot Yang Ming stomach channel acupoints
interventions.needle_size_exact: 45 mm in length and 0.3 mm in diameter, Suzhou Medical Appliance Factory, Jiangsu Province, China
interventions.penetration_exact: approximately 30 to 40 mm into the skin
interventions.manipulation_exact: needles in ST25, ST29, ST36, and ST40 connected to electro-stimulator (G6805-2 A, Shanghai Huayi Medicinal Instruments Co., Ltd, Shanghai, China) producing electrical stimulation with a continuous 1 Hz wave for 10 min
interventions.number_of_sessions_exact: once every 2 days, 15 times in total
interventions.practitioner_description_exact: professional acupuncturist with a Chinese medicine practitioner license from the Ministry of Health of the People's Republic of China
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: According to the theory of channels of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Foot Yang Ming stomach channel acupoints were chosen referring to previous systematic reviews and consultations with specialists

interventions.penetration_exact: needles were penetrated only 2-3 mm into the skin
interventions.manipulation_exact: needles in ST25, ST29, ST36, and ST40 were connected to the electro-stimulator without electrical stimulation

interventions.participant_instructions_exact: balanced diet providing energy deficit of 500 kcal per day; 45-60 E% carbohydrate, 15-20 E% protein, 20-35 E% fat (<7 E% saturated fat); exercise five times weekly at approximately 65% of peak heart rate gradually increased to 70 to 85%

extraction_notes.note: Expectancy, credibility, and blinding success were not assessed or reported in this study. No validated instruments (e.g., Credibility/Expectancy Questionnaire, Vincent's Acupuncture Credibility Scale) were used.
Deqi sensation was not measured or reported. The authors note in the Discussion/limitations that the sham needling 2-3mm depth can cause needle sensation, but no formal deqi instrument was used.

The exact number of participants analyzed for neuroimaging (rs-fMRI) is not reported in the paper. The text states the examination was conducted 'based on the principle of voluntariness' but does not give a specific N for fMRI analyses.

Text in Results (page 6) reports visceral fat area change as -6.23±9.06 cm2 for acupuncture group, but Table 2 (page 7) reports -8.95 (9.06). These values are inconsistent. The table value has been extracted in the primary outcome entry; the text value is noted here.
extraction_notes.source_location: Results: Change of body adipose tissue, page 6; Table 2, page 7

extraction_notes.note: Text in Results (page 6) reports body fat change as -0.99±1.63% for acupuncture group, but Table 2 (page 7) reports -1.28 (1.63). These values are inconsistent. The table value has been extracted; the text value is noted here.
extraction_notes.source_location: Results: Change of body adipose tissue, page 6; Table 2, page 7

extraction_notes.note: The paper reports preliminary thresholding for fALFF and ReHo as 'uncorrected p<0.005 with cluster-extent>=10 voxels' but the Table 3 caption states 'p<0.05, corrected for multiple comparisons' and Figure 2 caption states 'p<0.05, Bonferroni corrected'. The preliminary vs final threshold relationship is unclear from the text.
extraction_notes.source_location: Methods: MRI data analysis, page 4-5; Table 3, page 9; Figure 2 caption, page 8

extraction_notes.note: Table 3 reports p-values for individual brain regions (e.g., MOG_L p=0.047, R calcarine p=0.018) but these are reported in the Results text. The source of these individual region p-values is not clearly described in the statistical methods section — it is unclear whether these are post-hoc comparisons or ANOVA interaction terms.
extraction_notes.source_location: Results: Rs-fMRI activity alterations, page 7; Table 3, page 9

extraction_notes.note: The table label for 'Cuneus' in Table 3 (ReHo) does not specify hemisphere (the text says 'bilateral cuneus' p=0.034 but Table 3 lists a single coordinate row for Cuneus with no hemisphere designation). The x coordinate of 51 suggests right hemisphere, which conflicts with 'bilateral' in text.
extraction_notes.source_location: Results: Rs-fMRI activity alterations, page 7; Table 3, page 9

extraction_notes.note: Smoothing parameters (kernel size) for fMRI preprocessing are not explicitly stated beyond being step 6 of the preprocessing pipeline.
The depth_mm_numeric for sham needling was set to 2.5 as a midpoint of the reported '2-3 mm' range. This is a minor inferential step; exact value is 'only 2-3 mm into the skin'.

The paper does not report whether drug use (antidiabetic medications) differed between groups at baseline or at endpoint beyond stating 'differential analysis on drug use between the two groups did not display significance'. Specific drug types or proportions are not listed in the tables.

The exact n_analyzed for the rs-fMRI subsample is not reported. Only the text 'based on the principle of voluntariness' is given without a specific count. The MRI-PDFF/BIA subsample n=74 is explicitly reported.

The laterality stated in Table 3 for the fALFF result in 'L middle occipital gyrus' has x=21 (positive), which in standard MNI convention typically corresponds to the right hemisphere when left is negative. This appears to be an inconsistency in the paper between the region label ('L') and the coordinate sign (positive x=21 suggesting R hemisphere). Extracted as reported in the paper.
